top_story.headline: House Democrat Introduces Bill to Give Congress Power to End Military Exceptions to Posse Comitatus Act
top_story.dek: Rep. Patrick Ryan (D-NY-18) is the lead sponsor, with Democratic colleagues, of a bill on domestic use of the armed forces; it was one of 97 measures filed in a pro forma House session on Thursday, October 1, 2026.
paragraphs: H.R. 10697 would amend titles 18 and 10 of the United States Code to give Congress authority to terminate exceptions to the prohibition on using the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force and Space Force as a posse comitatus (a force for domestic law enforcement), according to its official title on Congress.gov..

Also filed that day was H.Res. 1596, a rule resolution from Rep. Jason Crow (D-CO-6) that would provide for House consideration of H.R. 9899, the Afghanistan TPS Act of 2026, which would designate Afghanistan for temporary protected status. That underlying bill was referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary on July 23, 2026; the rule resolution was referred to the House Committee on the Rules on October 1.

sections.headline: House Meets Briefly, Files 97 Measures and Adjourns to Monday; Senate Convenes
paragraphs: The House met at 11:30 a.m. on Thursday, October 1, 2026, with Rep. Dan Newhouse presiding as Speaker pro tempore, and adjourned at 11:33 a.m. until 4:30 p.m. on Monday, October 5, 2026, according to the Congressional Record for October 1. No votes appear in the record. The Record also notes the Speaker's September 29 signature on three Senate enrolled bills: S. 240 (Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Act of 2010 improvements), S. 283 (seafood country-of-origin standard) and S. 2403 (adequate consideration for closely held stock under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974).

The Senate met at 10:30 a.m. with Sen. Cynthia M. Lummis (R-WY) presiding; the Record shows only the opening entry for the Senate that day, with no bills or votes. All 97 House measures introduced are listed below: 80 bills, one joint resolution, one concurrent resolution and 15 simple resolutions. Most are routine or commemorative; the most substantive are the Posse Comitatus bill, the proposed constitutional amendment to abolish the electoral college (H.J.Res. 218 is listed below), and the Afghanistan rule resolution.
